title: Analyzing Polysomnography (PSG) Sleep Architecture & Hypnograms
description: Interpret a full-night hypnogram, quantifying NREM/REM cycle proportions and identifying pathological sleep fragmentation.
problemStatement:
You are a clinical neurophysiologist reviewing an overnight polysomnogram (PSG) and hypnogram of a 45-year-old corporate executive complaining of chronic morning exhaustion and brain fog.

### Your Mission:
1. **Hypnogram Profiling**: Describe the normal ultradian distribution of Slow-Wave Sleep (N3) vs. REM sleep across the first half of the night vs. the second half of the night.
2. **Pathology Identification**: The patient's hypnogram reveals zero Stage N3 slow-wave sleep, 45 micro-arousals per hour associated with complete cessation of airflow and oxygen desaturations to 82% (Obstructive Sleep Apnea).
3. **Cognitive & Glymphatic Repercussions**: Explain why the absence of N3 slow-wave sleep will specifically impair growth hormone secretion, declarative memory consolidation, and glymphatic brain clearance.
hints: Hint 1: Slow-wave sleep dominates the first third of the night, while REM periods lengthen substantially in the final third.
Hint 2: Repeated nocturnal hypoxemia and micro-arousals prevent the brain from sustaining continuous delta sleep epochs.
